samples.summary: An empty/partial font registry is reported as "settled", so a blocked or failed Google Fonts stylesheet passes silently with fallback glyphs
samples.evidence: `pending(families)` only iterates families that are *already registered* in `document.fonts`. If the `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...` stylesheet in `index.html` (or a lazily injected per-family link) never loads — DNS blocked, 4xx, offline runner — Chromium registers no @font-face rules at all for it, so `registry()` returns an empty (or Inter-less) Map, `pending()` returns `[]`, and `waitForFontsReady` returns success on attempt 0. The capture then paints the browser default serif, which is exactly the drift this PR exists to detect. Grep shows the frontend declares no local `@font-face` anywhere (only comments mention it), so with the CDN unreachable `document.fonts` is genuinely empty and the guard degenerates to a no-op. The same holds for `if (!document.fonts) return []` (line 377). Worse, in `UPDATE_VISUAL_BROWSER_BASELINE=true` mode the new "Refusing to record baselines from fallback glyphs" guard (line 640) never fires, so fallback-glyph baselines get committed. Needs an assertion that the expected Google Fonts links resolved / that at least the known-eager families are present, not just "nothing registered is missing".

samples.summary: Cache-busting param appended to the css2 URL may make Google Fonts return an error payload, dropping every @font-face and (with the finding above) turning failure into a silent pass
samples.evidence: `url.searchParams.set("wbVisualRetry", String(attempt))` rewrites the app's own `<link>` href in place. The comment asserts "css2 ignores it" with no verification; the css2 endpoint is documented as strict about its query grammar and can answer an invalid request with an error CSS body / non-200. If that happens, the refetch removes every previously-registered face from `document.fonts` (the old sheet is dropped when href changes), so the next settle sees an empty registry and returns `[]` — reported as success — and the app's link stays permanently pointed at the broken URL for the rest of that page's life. The recovery path can therefore convert a detected failure into an undetected one.

samples.summary: load() force-loads every registered family/weight, so any single slow or 404ing lazily-injected preview family fails the whole visual lane
samples.evidence: `load()` walks the entire registry (which includes families injected on demand by `ensureFontLink` for picker rows/previews, not only families the screenshot paints) and `pending()` requires each of them to reach `loaded` at every declared weight. A face in `status: "error"` (e.g. an arbitrary family whose css2 request 404s) can never recover, so `webFontFailures` is pushed and the run exits 1 (line 754) even when every pixel matched the baseline. The previous code only enumerated a fixed family list, so this newly couples the lane's exit code to the health of every family any harness component happens to touch.

samples.summary: Global "a face is still loading" check makes one unrelated in-flight subset face fail the entire run
samples.evidence: `if ([...document.fonts].some((face) => face.status === "loading")) missing.push("(a face is still loading)")` is evaluated over the whole registry, unfiltered by family or relevance. A single subset face still in flight at the 10s deadline (Google serves Korean families as ~100 subset faces) yields a non-empty `pending`, burns both refetches, and then records a permanent `webFontFailures` entry that exits the process 1 at line 754 — even though every family already had a `loaded` face and the screenshots are correct.

samples.summary: `fonts.load()` defaults to the single-space text, so families whose faces have no unicode-range covering U+0020 can never reach `loaded` and fail permanently
samples.evidence: `document.fonts.load(`${weight} 12px "${family}"`)` is called without a text argument; per spec the default text is " " (U+0020), so only the subset faces whose `unicode-range` contains the space character are fetched. `pending()` then demands `statuses.includes("loaded")` per family. Any registered family whose faces cover only non-latin ranges (a CJK/symbol-only subset payload) would stay `unloaded` forever, producing an unrecoverable failure that no refetch fixes and that exits the run 1.

samples.summary: The bounded `fonts.ready` race can consume the whole deadline, leaving the poll loop with zero iterations
samples.evidence: `await Promise.race([document.fonts.ready, sleep(Math.max(0, deadline - performance.now()))])` shares the same `deadline` as the poll below. If `fonts.ready` hangs (the case the comment cites as the reason to bound it), the race resolves exactly at the deadline, so `while (missing.length > 0 && performance.now() < deadline)` never executes a single tick — the pass reports `pending` without ever re-reading the registry, and jumps straight to a refetch it may not need.

samples.summary: `refetchPass` return value (number of matched links) is discarded, so a refetch that matched zero links looks identical to a real retry
samples.evidence: `await page.evaluate(refetchPass, attempt + 1)` at line 496 ignores the returned `links.length`. When no `link[rel='stylesheet']` points at fonts.googleapis.com (the very case where fonts failed because the link was never injected), the loop still spends another full 10s settle plus networkidle doing nothing, and the operator gets no signal that there was nothing to refetch.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. registry() (verify-visual-browser.mjs:385-396) derives the awaited set from document.fonts itself, and pending() (415-439) iterates only that registry-derived map, so a family that was never registered — the blocked/failed fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet at packages/frontend/index.html:12 — yields missing === []. waitForFontsReady then returns at 486 on attempt 0 without pushing to webFontFailures (490), so the end-of-run report (627-638) and the "Refusing to record baselines from fallback glyphs" bail-out (640-645), both gated on webFontFailures.length > 0, never fire; baselines are written at 665 via the real UPDATE_VISUAL_BROWSER_BASELINE=true path (line 15, packages/frontend/package.json:19, scripts/run-browser-tests-docker.sh:74). No positive/expected-family assertion exists anywhere in the script (grep for Inter/REQUIRED/VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES returns only comments), and refetchPass's links.length return (472) is discarded by the caller (496), so even "the stylesheet element loaded" is never verified. The frontend declares no local @font-face (only comments at verify-visual-browser.mjs:380 and src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:346), so with the CDN unreachable those families are genuinely absent from the registry. The repo's own note (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:75-76,89) claims this pairing makes an unreachable CDN fail, which holds only for registered families — confirming the gap rather than guarding it. Missing-guard / silent-failure / baseline-overwrite is squarely in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present verbatim: refetchPass rewrites the app's own css2 <link> href in place with an unverified `wbVisualRetry` param (verify-visual-browser.mjs:463-473), justified only by the comment "css2 ignores it" (:460-462). The consequence the reviewer describes is grounded in the surrounding logic and does not even depend on css2's exact query grammar: settlePass derives its awaited set solely from document.fonts (registry(), :385-396), so if the re-pointed sheet fails to load for any reason (400 on an unknown param, 429, network error) the CSS-connected faces are dropped, `families` is empty, load() queues nothing, pending() iterates zero families and returns [] (:399-456). The caller then treats [] as success, returns early and even logs "webfonts settled after N refetch(es)" (:480-487), so nothing reaches webFontFailures and the end-of-run failure gate (:627-645) and the visual:update refusal (:640-645) never fire — a detected font failure is converted into an undetected pass with fallback glyphs, and the link stays pointed at the broken URL. refetchPass runs only after a genuine pending failure (:496), i.e. exactly the state where masking is worst, and no guard checks that the registry survived the refetch (no empty-registry or families-shrank assertion anywhere in settlePass). The pixel-diff comparison is not a firm guard: sub-tolerance fallback rendering is the very failure mode this code exists to prevent (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:50-68). This is runtime logic of a gating verification script, so it is in the correctness lane, not test-quality. No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: New `.catch(() => {})` swallows font-fetch failures, and the claimed downstream detection does not exist
finding.evidence: `document.fonts.load(...).catch(() => {})` (line 374) now swallows every rejection. The adjacent comment asserts "a rejection here means the fetch failed, which the check pass below reports as a timeout naming the family", but `document.fonts.check()` (line 388) returns true whenever no registered FontFace matches the query (CSS fallback semantics) and for faces whose status has settled to `error`. So if fonts.googleapis.com is unreachable/blocked in CI — the very scenario the todo doc (docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-55) claims is now loudly reported — `check()` passes trivially, the catch-all poll at line 395 also passes (`status` is `error`/`unloaded`, not `loading`), and the harness silently screenshots fallback glyphs. Before this change the rejection propagated out of `page.evaluate` and failed the run loudly.

verdict.reason: The finding's central claim - that the new `.catch(() => {})` leaves only a vacuous `document.fonts.check()` as detection, so a failed font fetch silently screenshots fallback glyphs - is not the code in this tree. The cited line numbers do not match (the catch is at line 409, not 374), and `pending()` at verify-visual-browser.mjs:415-428 performs exactly the status-based detection the reviewer says does not exist: for each registered family it gathers the FontFace `status` values and requires `statuses.includes("loaded")`, pushing `family (error/unloaded/no faces)` into `missing` otherwise; the inline comment at 421-424 explicitly names the `check()`-is-vacuous semantics the reviewer argues were missed. `check()` at 429-433 is only a secondary per-weight assertion applied after the loaded-face bar. A swallowed rejection therefore still surfaces: the face settles to `error`, `pending()` reports it by name, the loop refetches the Google Fonts stylesheets (463-497), then records `webFontFailures` with a console.error, refuses `visual:update` (640-645) and exits non-zero (754-756). The failure is loud with artifacts, not silent. The only residual gap I could construct (a wholly blocked stylesheet leaving an empty `document.fonts` registry, so `registry()` at 385-396 has nothing to assert) is a different mechanism from the one claimed, and is documented as a known limitation in the todo doc.
